name: Grenaa
title: Ultrasonic Thickness Gauging Grenaa | Ro-Ro, Bulk & Recycling
description: Thickness gauging at Grenaa for ro-pax ferries, bulk ships, offshore wind vessels and ships heading for recycling: hull, hold, tank and deck UTM work.
h1: Thickness Measurement for Ferries, Bulk Ships and End-of-Life Vessels in Grenaa
intro: Grenaa, on the Kattegat coast of Djursland in east Jutland, combines a ferry link to Sweden with bulk and project cargo, an offshore wind service base and a ship recycling yard on the European list. That mix brings working ships that need routine gauging alongside vessels near the end of their trading lives, where readings help decide a final voyage or a sale. Atlantis keeps nobody at the port: for each ship, technicians travel from India and work aboard until the scope is complete.

highlights.p: Ships bound for the recycling yard at Grenaa sometimes need their condition confirmed before the last voyage or tow, and owners weighing a sale against recycling want to know what the next renewal survey would demand. Gauging gives both decisions a factual basis.

The ro-pax ferry across the Kattegat to Halmstad carries freight and cars on a fixed timetable. Car-deck, ramp and tank gauging is planned for its maintenance periods, with crack detection at door and ramp fittings that take load on every crossing.

Grenaa's harbour hosts the service base for the Anholt offshore wind farm in the Kattegat. Crew transfer and service vessels working from it see constant berthing loads, and fendering areas, deck fittings and fuel tanks benefit from periodic checks.

p: Grenaa sits on the east-facing coast of Djursland, the peninsula that pushes out from east Jutland into the Kattegat, and its harbour looks across open water towards the island of Anholt and the Swedish coast beyond. The approach is from the Kattegat, a busy sea crossed by the traffic between the Skagerrak and the Danish straits, where shallow banks and buoyed channels shape the routes that larger ships take past the area. The harbour itself is protected by breakwaters, has no meaningful tide and is generally ice-free, though strong easterly winds can make the entrance uncomfortable for smaller ships and slow cargo work on open quays. Ships bound for the harbour usually pick up a pilot or follow the marked approach from the open Kattegat, and the passage in is short once they leave the main traffic lanes.

Traffic at Grenaa is varied for a port of its size. A ro-pax ferry links the town with Halmstad in Sweden, and a smaller ferry serves Anholt. Bulk carriers and coasters bring in and take out agricultural products, feed, fertiliser, timber and other dry commodities for the Djursland hinterland, and project cargo moves over quays laid out with large storage areas. The harbour has also been a base for offshore wind since the Anholt wind farm was built in the Kattegat, and crew transfer and service vessels sail from Grenaa to the turbines. Fishing boats use the inner basins, so the harbour's working mix runs from small fishing boats to sea-going bulk carriers. Cargo calls are spread through the year, with agricultural shipments adding to the load after harvest.

The yard that sets Grenaa apart is Fornæs, a ship recycling facility on the European list under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation, which dismantles ships and other floating structures at the harbour. Vessels come here at the end of their working lives, some under their own power and others under tow, and each arrival has been preceded by decisions about condition, insurance, documentation and the voyage itself. For gauging, that creates a kind of work found in few other ports: measurements that support a final passage, or that inform an owner who is still deciding whether one more renewal survey is justified. Alongside it, the working fleets at Grenaa need the same routine gauging as anywhere else. Both kinds of job can be in the harbour on the same day.

facilities.h: Where gauging takes place at Grenaa
p: For the ferry and cargo trades, gauging is afloat work at the ship's own berth. The Halmstad ferry can be measured when it lies over at Grenaa outside the timetable or during planned maintenance, with car decks clear and tanks prepared by the crew. Bulk carriers and coasters at the cargo quays offer windows during discharge and loading: hatch covers, coamings, deck plating and accessible ballast tanks can be measured while cargo is worked in other holds, and empty holds can be gauged once discharge is complete. Crew transfer vessels and service ships at the wind-farm base are reached directly from the pontoons and quays they use between trips to the turbines.

Ships arriving at the recycling yard are a separate case. Once a ship has been delivered to the yard, its structure is the recycler's concern and gauging is rarely needed; the useful readings are taken before the voyage, often at the ship's last trading port, when the owner, the insurer or the surveyor assessing a tow wants assurance that the hull will hold together on the passage. Grenaa has no large dry dock for merchant ships, so dockings for the ferry and the cargo vessels go to yards elsewhere in Denmark or abroad, and readings taken alongside at Grenaa feed the yard's steel estimate before the ship arrives.
list: Ferry berth for the Halmstad route — car-deck, ramp, door-fitting and ballast tank gauging during lay-overs or planned maintenance.
Bulk and general cargo quays — hatch cover, coaming, hold and ballast tank readings on bulk carriers and coasters during discharge or loading.
Offshore wind service base — deck fittings, fendering structure and fuel tanks on crew transfer and service vessels between turbine trips.
Project cargo quays — tank-top and deck strengthening checks on heavy-lift ships after loading or discharging large components.
Recycling yard arrivals — condition readings arranged before the final voyage, at the ship's last port or lay-up position, when the voyage needs them.

context.h: Ship recycling rules, Kattegat trade and port state control
p: Denmark applies port state control under the Paris MoU through the Danish Maritime Authority, and as an EU state it applies the EU Ship Recycling Regulation. Under that regulation, EU-flagged ships may only be recycled at yards on the European list, of which Fornæs is one, and every ship above the size threshold calling at an EU port, whatever its flag, must carry an Inventory of Hazardous Materials. The IHM and the recycling plan are documentation tasks rather than thickness measurement, but they run alongside the condition decisions that gauging supports, and an owner planning a ship's last voyage to Grenaa deals with both at once. The Hong Kong Convention on ship recycling entered into force in June 2025, adding an international layer to the same process.

For the working fleets, the drivers are the familiar ones. The Halmstad ferry is inspected under the EU regime for ro-ro passenger ships on regular services as well as by class, and ships above the size threshold report emissions under the EU ETS, which has applied to shipping since 2024, and FuelEU Maritime, from 2025. Many of the bulk carriers calling at Grenaa are smaller short-sea ships, where corrosion in holds and ballast tanks is the main structural concern and where an intermediate or renewal survey can decide whether a ship keeps trading. Ice is rarely a factor in the Kattegat, though coasters that also load in the northern Baltic in winter carry ice-strengthened shell plating worth including in their plans.

jobs.p: Gauging requests at Grenaa come from three directions: the ferry operator planning maintenance, cargo-ship owners responding to a survey or a charterer's question, and owners deciding what to do with an ageing ship. That last group is particular to a port with a recycling yard, and the question they ask is practical: how much steel would the next survey require, and does the ship's condition support another period of trading or a sale for further use? We report readings against the class minimums and summarise the areas of substantial and excessive corrosion, so the owner can weigh the choice on measured condition rather than estimates.
list: A short-sea bulk carrier at the cargo quay: hold frames, hopper and topside tank plating and hatch coamings gauged ahead of its renewal survey.
The Halmstad ro-pax ferry during planned maintenance: car-deck plating, stern-ramp structure and ballast tanks measured, with MPI at ramp hinges.
An ageing general cargo ship whose owner is weighing renewal-survey steel against a sale: an owner's condition gauging of holds, tanks and deck.
Crew transfer and service vessels from the wind-farm base: fuel-tank and deck-fitting checks during a scheduled maintenance day.
Readings on a ship due to make a last voyage under tow, taken at its lay-up berth to support the towage surveyor's assessment.

logistics: Aarhus Airport, on Djursland between Aarhus and Grenaa, has limited international connections, so the team usually arrives through Copenhagen or Billund and continues by road or rail; the light-rail line from Aarhus ends at Grenaa. Denmark is in the Schengen area and the team needs Schengen visas issued in India, which take time to arrange. Port access is arranged by the ship's agent, and work at the recycling yard or the wind-farm base follows that site's own safety rules.

faqs.q: Do ships going to the Grenaa recycling yard need thickness measurement?
faqs.a: Not always. Gauging is needed when someone involved in the last voyage asks for it: an insurer, a towage or warranty surveyor, the flag or class where the ship is still classed, or the owner. Those readings are usually taken before the ship sails, at its last trading port or lay-up berth, and concentrate on the structure that matters for the passage, such as shell, main deck and watertight bulkheads.

faqs.q: Can an owner use gauging to decide between another survey and recycling?
faqs.a: Yes, and that is often the most valuable use of readings on an older ship. An owner's condition gauging before the renewal survey shows how much plating and framing would need renewal, which areas are close to their limits and where pitting or grooving is advancing. With that, the owner can compare the yard work required against the ship's trading outlook or a sale for further use.

faqs.q: Can bulk carriers be gauged during discharge at Grenaa?
faqs.a: Partly. Hatch covers, coamings, deck plating and ballast tanks the crew has opened can be measured while cargo is worked, and each hold can be gauged once it is empty and clean enough for safe access. Holds still holding cargo or under active grab discharge are not entered. We sequence the work with the stevedores and the chief officer so that readings follow the discharge.

faqs.q: Is there a dry dock in Grenaa?
faqs.a: Not for merchant ships of any size, so dockings for the ferry and for cargo ships calling here are booked at yards elsewhere. Gauging done alongside at Grenaa before the docking gives the yard and the class surveyor a steel estimate in advance, and the team can continue at the docking yard if the owner wants the renewal-survey programme completed there.
